title: Canonical models and the whole-system projection-word reduction square
statement:
Let $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ have characteristic $p$, let $\ell\ne p$ be prime, and fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside the coefficient algebraic closure [def-pur-conventions]. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and fix a compactification $f=p\circ j:X\to Y$ with $j$ open and $p$ proper, where $f$ is smooth of pure relative dimension $d\ge0$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Fix the actual strict coefficient towers, operation and coordinate models, normalized reduction equivalences and the specified tower adjunction and finite-level comparisons [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers, det-sp-tower-gamma, det-sp-integral-adjunction-bijection]. There exist a realization $r$ and finite-Tor preservation certificates for its compact support $P$ and right adjoint $H$, simultaneous normalized completed-operation models $m$, a coefficient-stage exceptional RingSystem $S$ with its Hom-normalized finite comparison, the normalized completed pullback of the unit, and K-flat coefficient-unit comparisons $\mu_X,\mu_Y$ [def-pur-realized-tower-purity-data].

For every specified adjunction $P\dashv G$ on the common finite-Tor category, the canonical source and exceptional realization isomorphisms exist. The source isomorphism is SourceNormalized on every K-flat representative, the exceptional isomorphism has exactly the specified scalar-mate reduction, and their finite purity composite has the actual finite purity maps at every positive uniformizer exponent, as in the finite-reduction part of [def-pur-realized-tower-purity-data]. Put $T=\mathbf1_X(d)[2d]$, $\omega=G\mathbf1_Y$, $a=\Gamma_{\mathbf1_Y}$ and $R_K=P(\sigma_K)P(1\otimes a)\Pi_{K,\omega}(1\otimes\epsilon_{\mathbf1_Y})\rho_K$, where $\Pi$ is inverse projection, with source-unit identification understood. The source and inner completion units for $T,\omega$, the coefficient right-unit completion and $\sigma_K$ are invertible. Whenever the two projections are invertible, the following identity is an identity of entire strict derived towers:
$$\operatorname{reduceWord}(R_K)=\operatorname{towerProjection}(K).$$
Here towerProjection is the explicit $b_D$, source comparison, diagonal orientation and tower projection/counit composite of [def-pur-realized-tower-purity-data], not a reduction of $P(\Gamma_K)\epsilon_K$. In addition inverse projection is natural in every ambient second-input map $u:T\to\omega$:
$$P(1\otimes u)\Pi_{K,\omega}=\Pi_{K,T}(1\otimes Pu).$$
The theorem does not assert invertibility or naturality of $\Gamma_K$, its whole-system exceptional reduction equation, or either integral adjunct identity. Those follow in the parent by categorical transposition, reconstruction, faithfulness and tensor functoriality.

Write ell=u*pi^e and first apply completed-operation substitution in uniformizer coordinates; then restrict whole diagrams to e(n+1), preserving quotient projections and augmentations. Fix the source comparison by these operations and the ordered Tate-line comparison. K-flat tensor collapse fixes the source and coefficient-unit normalization, including d=0.

proof.text: Apply the compactification projection reduction square with the pinned reconstruction comparison b, on both T and H(1), then transfer the latter to G(1) by its counit-preserving isomorphism. Its hypotheses hold because T and H(1) are isomorphic shifted Tate lines and the source reductions have the common Tor bounds. Reduce the right-hand projection word R_K, move c across inverse projection by naturality, and insert the actual counit-reduction and unit-orientation equations. The tensor/pullback source factors become q_K, so the resulting composite is exactly towerProjection, without transposing gamma.
